items.evidence: Paragraph 196 expressly disclaims an innocence finding and then uses emphatic Rule-of-Law rhetoric to condemn inconsistency, concealment and inequities in this investigation.
items.scope_review: Qualification: the passage is current-court evaluative language, not mere neutral editorial text. The hard negative remains preferable because it supplies no new legal test or operative disposition beyond the already explicit procedural-fairness holding; consumers must not misread the label as non-court speech.

items.evidence: Paragraph 95 attributes both the admission of serious consequences and the defence of procedural sufficiency to the respondent.
items.scope_review: The court's correctness/fairness analysis starts in paragraph 96.

items.evidence: Paragraph 54 states that intent is essential to the evidence analysis and that the material fact alone is insufficient.
items.scope_review: Paragraph 53 provides the fraud/deception context and exact good-faith/error exception. The later Commission quotation is not used as court proposition evidence.

items.evidence: Paragraph 61 says it is highly relevant, in assessing this decision's reasonableness, to verify whether the Commission applied and considered its own false-reference jurisprudence.
items.scope_review: Qualification: this is analytical guidance, not a final jurisdiction or reasonableness holding. The jurisdiction assumption in paragraph 61 and the paragraph-93 no-definitive-opinion limit are indispensable; removing either would materially overstate the AU. Both exact witnesses are present.

items.scope_review: The target does not endorse general authority to impose those measures; the contested jurisdiction analysis follows.
